This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in businessUnitIsLive; a string literal in expandBusinessUnitUsers), sys_team (literal, a string literal in readTeamRow; a string literal in teamIsProvablyOutsideOrg))_

- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in businessUnitIsLive; a string literal in expandBusinessUnitUsers))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in businessUnitIsLive; a string literal in expandBusinessUnitUsers))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in businessUnitIsLive; a string literal in expandBusinessUnitUsers))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `100d782f466c11b61086327f2f85b292858aa07f` — the merge of head `f9f2b6f89205cc07b05c3e3a981ca419784b067a` into base `dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 100d782f466c11b61086327f2f85b292858aa07f && git checkout 100d782f466c11b61086327f2f85b292858aa07f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42 f9f2b6f89205cc07b05c3e3a981ca419784b067a && git checkout -B drift-repro dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42 && git merge --no-ff f9f2b6f89205cc07b05c3e3a981ca419784b067a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3eb0a962bb94a01225956da313663e5a1bcc15d0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.test.ts + packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts (`handleApprovalError`, `decisionRoute`), packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts on `main` (`DecisionOutputDefSchema`, `normalizeDecisionOutputs`, the `decisionOutputs` docblock), docs/adr/0104-field-runtime-value-shape-contract.md (the 2026-10-30 amendment under D2 item 1), examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/dynamic-approval.flow.ts, content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx on `main`, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`buildApiActionRequest`, the `outputs.KEY` fold), ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/decisionOutputParams.ts and ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts (the Console's decision dialog, read as the first consumer of the narrowed door)

Face: narrowing. The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at the start of a line, and the ruling 6566731522 on #28658 declares the narrowing. No path under `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path is in the file list. Check-runs on this head: every run is `completed`; every conclusion is `success` or `skipped`; none failed and none is still running.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set change the diff implies, judged against the ruling and the code it cites.

1. `user` output: a value must be a `sys_user` record id (`reassignTargetRefusal(value, null)`, no organization screen). **Right.** It is the predicate the downstream `resolveAs: 'user'` reader asks (`namesNoAccount`, #27397), so the decision refuses exactly what that reader would drop. A user of another organization passes here and routes there too; that asymmetry with the three graph kinds is the downstream reader's, not this diff's.
2. `user` output: a slot address (`KIND:VALUE`) or an email is refused as "not a user id". **Right by the ruling's letter** ("`user` ... by record id"). Note: the downstream reader would accept an email and route to it (`reassignTargetRefusal` resolves `email`), so this refuses a value the next step could use. The ruling asked for ids; the record notes the gap, no fix.
3. `department` output: an active `sys_business_unit` of the request's organization (`businessUnitIsLive`, extracted from `expandBusinessUnitUsers`). **Right.** The extraction keeps the expansion's behaviour: the seed check still returns `[]` on a failed read (the `try/catch` stays at the call site). A request with no organization keeps the unfiltered read, as before.
4. `team` output: a `sys_team` row exists and is not provably another organization's (`readTeamRow`, extracted from `teamIsProvablyOutsideOrg`). **Right.** The extraction keeps the screen's behaviour: a failed read still answers `false` at the call site; a row with no `organization_id` passes, as before. Members are not checked; the ruling says "by record id", so this matches.
5. `position` output: a machine name someone in the request's organization holds (`expandPositionUsers`, which also unions `sys_member.role` tiers). **Right.** It is the only position resolver the `expression` approver has; a `sys_position` id names no holder and is refused, as the spec docblock on `main` already warns. A membership tier name such as `owner` passes as a "position"; the downstream reader treats it the same way.
6. `multiple: true` takes an array and only an array; `multiple` absent or `false` takes a non-array. **Right for the four picker kinds.** For `text` and bare keys, see ④ finding 1: it is within the ruling's letter but it breaks the shipped Console.
7. A list with one entry twice is refused, for pickers and for text. **Right.** The ruling names duplicates. Entries differing by whitespace or case are not merged; a non-identical picker entry then fails resolution on its own, so nothing slips through as a hidden duplicate.
8. A non-string or blank-string picker entry is refused ("must hold ... as text"). **Right.**
9. A blank value (`''`, `[]`, `null`, `undefined`) is skipped and left to `required`. **Right.** The same `isBlankDecisionOutput` predicate decides both, so the two checks cannot disagree.
10. A reject carrying a mismatched output is refused; a reject with none is unchanged. **Right.** `decideNode` snapshots and resumes with the outputs on a reject too, and the ruling speaks of any admitted output.
11. A failed directory read refuses nothing. **Right and consistent** with every resolver in the file. It makes the guarantee best-effort, which the changeset says.
12. Order: the check runs after the `required` check and before `assertRunResumable` and the first `engine.insert`. **Right.** Nothing is written before a refusal; a mid-tally vote is judged before it is counted.
13. A CSV string for a `multiple: true` output is now refused. **Right to refuse** (a string is not a list), but the spec docblock on `main` (approval.zod.ts L1211-1213) spells CSV out as accepted, and the changeset does not name it. See ② should-fix.
14. Refusal code `VALIDATION_FAILED`, mapped to 400 by `handleApprovalError` (packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts L126). **Right.** The ruling's `VALIDATION_ERROR` is ADR-0104 D2's action-params code; the approvals door has one validation code and the sibling `required` refusal uses it. Seat answer Q1 = A is right.
15. Public surface: no export, type or schema changes. The two new methods and two extracted helpers are `private`; `teamOrganizationOf` and `DECISION_OUTPUT_VALUE_NOUN` are module-local. **Right.** `businessUnitIsLive` drops the `as any` on the find options; typecheck is green on this head.

### ② Semver level

- Package and level: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` at `patch`, with `!` in the summary and a BREAKING banner. **Right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: a non-protocol change, breaking or not, ships `patch` and keeps its banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The diff moves no other released package.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset. **Right.** The approve and reject doors refuse payloads they admitted before; nothing is widened.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. **Right**, and this answers the dev's round-2 question. The kind grades what a metadata author can write. This diff refuses no authored key or value and changes no default's declared meaning: on `main` the `multiple` describe already says "stored as a list", so an absent `multiple` already declared one value; the docblock only said the runtime did not check it. What changes is the request door's acceptance of a decision payload, which is the narrowing arm's subject, not the protocol line's. `semantic` would be owed if the absent default's declared meaning moved; its enforcement moved, not its meaning. The ruling fixed these two lines and the diff matches them.
- The seat's answer on record ("`multiple` binds every declaration, text and bare keys included, shape only for text") is within the ruling's text: the `multiple` sentence names no kind, and the acceptance names "a scalar where a list is declared". But it reaches a consumer the ruling did not weigh. See ④ finding 1.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. **Should-fix.** The gate passed, but statement against statement the body contradicts the parenthetical: "A step whose bare-key output collects a list declares it `{ key: 'KEY', multiple: true }`" is an instruction to rewrite authored metadata, which the category says a changeset claiming it cannot carry. Either reword the remedy so it is not a rewrite prescription (state that a bare key takes one value, as its declaration always said, and that a CSV string still reaches the downstream `expression` reader as a list), or pick the disposition that admits the rewrite. No mechanical migration exists (no conversion can know which bare keys carried lists), so the reword is the honest path.
- Changeset prose. **Should-fix**, three sentences owed: (a) the "Before" should name the CSV string the spec on `main` admits for a list output, since it is now refused; (b) the remedy should say what an approver does with a request already pending under a bare-key snapshot in `node_config_json`, which no re-declaration reaches: send one value (a CSV string, which the downstream reader splits); (c) "Who sees it" should name an author who pairs a picker output with an `organization`-retargeted `expression` approver (ADR-0105 D9), whose directory organization the decision cannot know.
- `Skills-docs:` line. **Should-fix.** The pm-dispatch skill owes the PR body a `Skills-docs:` line for a `(narrowing)` arm; the body has none. The seat's checklist would REWORK on it; the record names it so the body is corrected with the rest.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and `open_questions`, each answered.

- Q1 (round 1), refusal code: **A, keep `VALIDATION_FAILED`.** One door, one validation code; the ruling's spelling is a slip the spec slice (#29340, correction 6578262566) already carries.
- Q2 (round 1), organization for graph kinds: **A, the request's organization, accepted for this head.** No declaration ties an output to one downstream approver, so the decision has nothing else to resolve in. The limit is real for an author who retargets stage 2 with `organization` (ADR-0105 D9); name it in the changeset (② should-fix c). Not a fix on this head.
- Q3 (round 1), position by holders: **A.** The ruling says "the same resolvers the expression approver already uses", and that approver has only the holder expansion. A held name is the only value that does not route to nobody.
- Q4 (round 1, seat answered B in round 2), `multiple` on `text`: the seat's reading is within the ruling's text, but landing it as delivered breaks the shipped Console for a schema-valid declaration. **Escalated as ④ finding 1, must-fix.** The seat, or the maintainer if the seat reads the ruling as binding text now, chooses between the two exits named there.
- Round-2 question, `Metadata-protocol: semantic` with a migration note: **A, `none` stands**, for the reasons in ②. The ADR-0087 parenthetical and the remedy wording are the part to reconcile (② should-fix).
- Dev deviation, forced test edits: the four edits are each a test whose fixture never named a real record or sent a list under a bare key. **Accepted.** They are consequences of the narrowing, not test weakening; the new tests pin the refusals the old fixtures would now hit.
- Dev deviation, ablation legs at older heads: `approval-service.ts` at `3eb0a962` differs from `59bdcb56` (the text branch was added in round 2), and the dev ran two new legs at `3eb0a962` for that branch. The round-1 legs cover unchanged code. **Accepted**; the record relies on the check-runs, not on these readings.
- Landing order: the ruling lands the spec text slice first. PR #29371 (card #29340) is open and draft at `fc024e80`; this PR waits for it. The two texts agree on this head's behaviour (text judged by shape, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, reject judged).
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the ruling and the published spec on `main`. Cases tried:

- A decision written before any check: no. Every refusal in `decideNode` precedes the `sys_approval_action` insert; the new check sits between `required` and `assertRunResumable`. The end-to-end test asserts the action rows stay `['submit']`, the request `pending`, the run suspended.
- A reject path: judged when outputs are present, unchanged when absent. Right; the outputs ride the reject's resume and snapshot.
- A multi-approver node: a co-sign vote is judged before the tally reads or writes anything; `pending_approvers` is unchanged on refusal. Right.
- A position name vs a `sys_position` id: the id is refused with a message that says a position is named by its machine name. Right, and it matches the docblock on `main` that already warned an id "would expand to nobody".
- A cross-organization id: `department`, `team`, `position` are screened in the request's organization; `user` is not, as its downstream reader is not. Right by the readers' own contracts.
- Duplicates after normalisation: identical strings only. A whitespace or case variant of a picker id fails resolution on its own, so no hidden duplicate passes. For text, `['a', 'a ']` passes as two values; acceptable, text has no reader that merges them.
- An output not declared: refused by the existing undeclared-key check before this one. Unchanged.
- The request staying pending with no decision row: holds, by the order above.
- The flow never seeing a dead approver: holds for `user` and `position`. For `team` and `department` the check proves the record, not its members; an empty team or department still reaches `onEmptyApprovers` downstream. This is what the ruling asked for ("by record id"), so it is noted, not a finding.
- A failed read: passes, so the guarantee is best-effort. Consistent with the file; the changeset says so.

Findings:

1. **Must-fix. The head refuses the payload the shipped Console sends for a `text` output declared `multiple: true`, and the Console has no other way to send it.** Read in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/decisionOutputParams.ts`: every non-picker output, typed `text` or a bare key, renders as a `type: 'text'` param with no `multiple`, under the help text "Handed to the flow as a decision output. Comma-separate multiple values." (`ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` L148). `foldDecisionOutputs` and `buildApiActionRequest` pass that one string through unchanged. On `main` the string is accepted and the downstream `expression` approver splits it (`csvSplit`), so a text `multiple: true` output worked from the Console. At this head `assertDecisionOutputsMatchDeclarations` refuses it: "`outputs.KEY` takes a list of values (it is declared `multiple: true`), not a single value". The step can then be decided only through the API. The shape is schema-valid (`multiple` is allowed on every type), and the spec slice #29371 makes `{ key: 'next_reviewers', multiple: true }` the docs page's headline example, so after both land the documented flow cannot be decided from the Console. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 4 ships a change that breaks `ui/` together with the `ui/` fix or not at all. Two exits, the seat's or the maintainer's call: (a) the Console companion lands with this PR by ruling (the text widget sends an array when `multiple: true`; the card currently bars `ui/**`); or (b) the shape check binds the four picker kinds now and `text` and bare keys only once the Console can send a list, with the seat's Q4 answer and the #29371 text revised to match. Either way the tree as it stands must not land.
2. **Should-fix.** The ADR-0087 parenthetical and the remedy paragraph contradict each other (② above). Reword the remedy or change the disposition.
3. **Should-fix.** The changeset's "Before", remedy and "Who sees it" owe the three sentences named in ② (CSV string now refused; the in-flight request under a bare-key snapshot; the `organization`-retargeted stage 2).
4. **Should-fix.** The PR body owes the `Skills-docs:` line for its `(narrowing)` arm.
5. Noted, no fix: `user` refuses an email the downstream reader would route to; `team` and `department` prove the record and not its members; a membership tier name passes as a `position`. Each matches the ruling's letter or the downstream reader's contract, and the record names them so the next reader does not re-derive them.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c7ca5d18fa2eddbf9fda9f6b736954f18127b9f6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the round-3 delta `3eb0a962..c7ca5d18` less the `origin/main` merge `4da16f2a2`, which is the 19-file PR file list GitHub reports: ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/decisionOutputParams.ts (+ .test.ts), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.decisionOutputList-28658.test.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/DeclaredActionsBar.test.tsx, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/{ar,de,en,es,fr,ja,ko,pt,ru,zh}.ts, .changeset/28658-console-decision-output-list.md (new), .changeset/28658-decision-output-type-multiple.md (reworded), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts (two tests). Re-read for the fold faces: ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx (the Approval Center api handler's `outputs.KEY` fold), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`buildApiActionRequest`'s fold), packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-forward.test.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/TagsField.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/paramValueShape.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts (`TranslationKeys`), packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts on `main` after #29371. `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`, `approval-node.test.ts` and `packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts` are byte-identical to `3eb0a962` (`git diff --stat` empty), so the prior record's ① judgments 1-15 stand unchanged and are not re-derived here.

Face: narrowing, as before. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand at the start of a line in the PR body (L7-8) and in both changesets (28658-decision-output-type-multiple.md L7-8; 28658-console-decision-output-list.md L8-9). The PR body now also carries `Skills-docs: follow-up #29512 — skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` (L10); #29512 is open, labelled `documentation` / `pm:queue` / `domain:skills`. No `packages/spec/**` path and no governed path is in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success). Check-runs on this head: every run `completed`; every conclusion `success` or `skipped`; none failed, none in progress. `Check Changeset`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI (1-16/16)`, `Test Core (1-8/8)`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `PR-body guards` are all `success`; the skipped ones are opt-in or schedule-gated (`18.x upgrade harness`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Schedule gate`).

### ① Derived judgments

The prior record's ④ finding 1 and ② should-fixes, each against the lines that answer it; then the Console's accept-set faces.
